title: 1.1 Data, Information, Knowledge, and Wisdom
description: Differences between data, information, knowledge and wisdom

questions.question: What is data?
options: Raw facts that cannot give meaning on its own
Processed facts presented to end users
The highest level of human understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Raw facts that cannot give meaning on its own

questions.question: Which of the following is considered data?
options: A wise decision about a business

questions.question: Data is recorded and stored using which forms?
Which of the following is better represented by numbers than by texts?
Words such as name are only represented by which form?
What is information?
options: A set of instructions for the computer
The highest level of human understanding
Data processed in a meaningful way to the end users
Raw facts that give no meaning on their own
questions.correctAnswer: Data processed in a meaningful way to the end users

questions.question: Daily sales data must be aggregated by what period to turn it into information?
Asking relevant questions about which of the following helps derive valuable information from data?
In which forms can information be represented?
options: Table, line graph, bar graph, or formulas
questions.correctAnswer: Table, line graph, bar graph, or formulas

questions.question: What is knowledge?
options: Raw facts that give no meaning on their own
An understanding acquired by further processing and integrating different sets of information
questions.correctAnswer: An understanding acquired by further processing and integrating different sets of information

questions.question: Knowledge includes both understanding and what?
When you tell a child how to ride a bicycle, what are you giving the child?
When a child applies information in riding a bicycle and acquires the necessary skills, the information becomes what?
Knowledge is acquired by integrating information from which of the following sources?
options: Reading books, engaging in different activities, and discussing with other people
questions.correctAnswer: Reading books, engaging in different activities, and discussing with other people

questions.question: Knowledge is the capability to think and act in order to do what?
options: Solve a problem or accomplish a given task
questions.correctAnswer: Solve a problem or accomplish a given task

questions.question: The ability to read this textbook or maintain a computer is an example of what?
Which of the following is more of a personal possession that you retrieve and apply when you need it?
What is wisdom?
options: The ability to make wise decisions and judgments using one's knowledge
A series of steps to achieve a goal
The physical parts of an information system
Raw facts stored in a database
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to make wise decisions and judgments using one's knowledge

questions.question: Wisdom is the highest level of what?
Wisdom is associated with good judgment and what?
options: Actions that contribute to living well
questions.correctAnswer: Actions that contribute to living well

questions.question: According to the text, wisdom is like which of the following?
Which thinking types are included in wisdom?
options: Intuitive, logical, creative, and collective thinking
questions.correctAnswer: Intuitive, logical, creative, and collective thinking

questions.question: Data, information, knowledge, and wisdom can be arranged in which of the following ways?
options: In a hierarchy with wisdom at the bottom
In a hierarchy with data at the bottom and wisdom at the top
In a circle with no order
questions.correctAnswer: In a hierarchy with data at the bottom and wisdom at the top

questions.question: As you move up in the data-to-wisdom pyramid, what happens to the value you get?
The top of the pyramid is where we have turned knowledge and insights into what?
In the difference section, data is described as anything represented as what?
When we say that +251********* is a person's phone number, the data becomes what?
Which of the following refers to understanding patterns, rules, or other mechanisms that serve as a guide for our future actions?
